headline: Security alert: Pipe bomb planted to target Rath Yatra
summary: Authorities have uncovered a plot to disrupt the religious procession, raising security concerns.
details: A pipe bomb was discovered and neutralized by security forces, having been planted to target the Rath Yatra procession.
The discovery has led to increased security measures to ensure the safety of devotees and participants in the religious event.
Security agencies are currently investigating the search for the suspects responsible for planting the device.
This incident highlights the ongoing efforts by law enforcement to prevent potential threats to public gatherings and religious festivals.

headline_marked: Over 90% death rate: [[Drug-resistant bacteria spread in ICUs]], icddr,b finds
headline: Over 90% death rate: Drug-resistant bacteria spread in ICUs, icddr,b finds
summary: A study by icddr,b reveals that more than 90% of ICU patients infected with these bacteria die, while 53% acquire the infection during their hospital stay.
details: A new study by icddr,b has found that drug-resistant bacteria are spreading within Intensive Care Units (ICUs), posing a severe threat to critically ill patients.
The findings are alarming: more than 90% of ICU patients infected with these drug-resistant bacteria died.
Furthermore, 53% of ICU patients acquired these dangerous bacteria during their stay at the hospital, indicating a significant risk of hospital-acquired infections.
The study highlights that these bacteria can spread from one patient to another within hospital environments, increasing the risk for those already in critical condition.
However, the research also demonstrates the impact of better infection prevention. Implementing training, hand hygiene, and maintaining a clean environment can drastically reduce risks.
According to icddr,b, better infection prevention measures can lead to an 86% reduction in bloodstream infections and an 85% reduction in deaths.
caption:
Over 90% of ICU patients infected with drug-resistant bacteria die. This is a silent crisis in our hospitals.

A new study by icddr,b has found that drug-resistant bacteria are spreading within Intensive Care Units (ICUs), posing a severe threat to critically ill patients.

The findings are alarming: more than 90% of ICU patients infected with these drug-resistant bacteria died.

Furthermore, 53% of ICU patients acquired these dangerous bacteria during their stay at the hospital, indicating a significant risk of hospital-acquired infections.

The study highlights that these bacteria can spread from one patient to another within hospital environments, increasing the risk for those already in critical condition.

However, the research also demonstrates the impact of better infection prevention. Implementing training, hand hygiene, and maintaining a clean environment can drastically reduce risks.

According to icddr,b, better infection prevention measures can lead to an 86% reduction in bloodstream infections and an 85% reduction in deaths.
